scope: Twelve exact chemistry-coded cards; current route preparation and co-requisites remain separate from degree requirements. No cross-list equivalence inferred from CHEM/ENVS/PUBL shared titles.

CHMG-141.name: General & Analytical Chemistry I
CHMG-141.description: Empirical chemical science, conceptual/visual/mathematical models, atomic structure, bonds and chemical reactions, with introductory organic connections.

category_review.locator: CHMG-141 complete current rendered course card
category_review.rationale: The full content concerns chemical structure and transformations; mathematical models support chemistry.

CHMG-145.name: General & Analytical Chemistry I Lab
CHMG-145.description: Laboratory techniques and data analysis using gravimetric, volumetric, thermal, titration and spectrophotometric methods.
CHMG-145.prerequisites: Prerequisite or Co-requisite: CHMG-141 or CHMG-131 or equivalent course.

category_review.locator: CHMG-145 complete current rendered course card
category_review.rationale: The course practices experimental chemical analysis, not generic statistical or computational methods.

CHMG-142.name: General & Analytical Chemistry II
CHMG-142.description: Thermodynamics and kinetics of chemical reactions, energy/entropy, solutions, acid-base and solubility equilibria, and redox processes.
CHMG-142.prerequisites: Prerequisites: CHMG-141 or CHMG-131 or equivalent course.

category_review.locator: CHMG-142 complete current rendered course card
category_review.rationale: Chemical equilibrium, energy and reaction rates are the substantive science domain.

CHMG-146.name: General & Analytical Chemistry II Lab
CHMG-146.description: Experimental chemical analysis and formal reporting using titration, pH/buffers, redox kinetics and electrochemical techniques.
CHMG-146.prerequisites: Prerequisites: CHMG-131 or CHMG-141 or equivalent course. Corequisites: CHMG-142 or equivalent course.

category_review.locator: CHMG-146 complete current rendered course card
category_review.rationale: Chemical laboratory investigation is primary; reporting supports the experimental work.

CHMG-131.name: General Chemistry for Engineers
CHMG-131.description: Chemical concepts, stoichiometry, thermodynamics/thermochemistry, electronic structure and bonding with workshop problems. Primarily intended for engineering students but explicitly not limited to them.

category_review.locator: CHMG-131 complete current rendered course card
category_review.rationale: The description teaches chemistry to an engineering-oriented but nonexclusive audience.

CHMO-231.name: Organic Chemistry I
CHMO-231.description: Organic structure, naming, synthesis, bonding, spectroscopy, stereochemistry and reaction mechanisms for initial functional-group families.
CHMO-231.prerequisites: Prerequisites: CHMG-142 or CHMG-131 or equivalent course. Corequisites: CHMO-235 or equivalent course.

category_review.locator: CHMO-231 complete current rendered course card
category_review.rationale: Organic chemistry and chemical reaction mechanisms are the course subject.

CHMA-211.name: Quantitative Analysis
CHMA-211.description: Quantitative chemical methods, gravimetry, equilibria, solution chemistry, electrochemistry and potentiometry, including statistical methods.
CHMA-211.prerequisites: Prerequisites: (CHEM-172 & CHEM-176) or (CHMG-142 & CHMG-146) or (CHEM-151 & CHEM-155) or equivalent courses. Co-requisites: CHMA-215 or equivalent course.

category_review.locator: CHMA-211 complete current rendered course card
category_review.rationale: Quantification is directed to chemical analysis and equilibria; statistical methods are one supporting component.

CHMA-311.name: Instrumental Analysis
CHMA-311.description: Theory and implementation of spectroscopy, mass spectrometry and chemical separations, including gas/liquid chromatography.
CHMA-311.prerequisites: Prerequisites: CHMA-211 or CHMA-161 or CHMG-142 or equivalent course. Co-requisites: CHMA-315 or equivalent course.

category_review.locator: CHMA-311 complete current rendered course card
category_review.rationale: The description concerns chemical measurement instruments and analytical techniques.

CHMB-402.name: Biochemistry I
CHMB-402.description: Biological macromolecular structure/function and metabolism, protein catalysis, membranes and physical principles of metabolic processes.
CHMB-402.prerequisites: Prerequisite: CHMO-231 or CHMO-331 or equivalent course.

category_review.locator: CHMB-402 complete current rendered course card
category_review.rationale: Biomolecular chemistry and metabolism are the central domain.

CHMI-351.name: Descriptive Inorganic Chemistry
CHMI-351.description: Inorganic reactions and periodic trends, bonding and solid-state structures, nanomaterials and industrial/environmental applications.
CHMI-351.prerequisites: Prerequisite: CHMO-231 or CHMO-331 or equivalent course.

category_review.locator: CHMI-351 complete current rendered course card
category_review.rationale: Inorganic chemical reactions, materials and structures dominate the course.

CHMO-232.name: Organic Chemistry II
CHMO-232.description: Organic structure, naming, reactions and synthesis for aromatic, alcohol, ether, epoxide and carbonyl functional groups, using reaction mechanisms.
CHMO-232.prerequisites: Prerequisites: CHMO-231 or CHMO-331 or equivalent course. Corequisites: CHMO-236 or equivalent course.

category_review.locator: CHMO-232 complete current rendered course card
category_review.rationale: The full description continues organic chemical transformations and synthesis.

CHEM-531.name: Climate Change: Science Technology & Policy
CHEM-531.description: Multidisciplinary climate change, including atmospheric chemistry, models, ecological effects, economics, international policy and social/environmental justice.
CHEM-531.prerequisites: This class is restricted to undergraduate students with at least 3rd year standing.

category_review.locator: CHEM-531 complete current rendered course card
category_review.rationale: The explicit multidisciplinary survey combines substantive climate science/ecology with economic, policy and justice analysis; neither primary domain can safely displace the other.
